analysis:
Examined the base text of .github/scripts/test-threat-budget.py (lines 1-1083). It is offline CI test code for the threat-review budget, cache and escalation tooling. It does not touch provider, coordinator, attestation, encryption or cache runtime assets (A-001..A-017, TB-002/003/007/009/010/011, T-041). Changed ranges are confined to test expectations.

Base 664/671 is renamed and now expects [SONNET, SONNET] instead of [SONNET, SONNET, OPUS] when only Sonnet integration is uncertain. The test still asserts that manual_review_reasons is non-empty and that clean() is False. The escalation policy therefore drops a redundant local Opus depth pass, but uncertainty still blocks a clean merge.

Head lines 949-982 add two tests:
- A manual GitHub rerun (GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT=2) must perform no paid work, must not start source collection, and must hand off to human review with clean()=False.
- A runtime bound of fifty minutes.

Both changes are fail-closed in intent. No secrets appear; synthetic tokens only.

No product security regression was identified. Whether the actual implementation in budget_scan/budget_runner enforces these behaviors lies outside the supplied evidence. Integration should confirm that the removed Opus depth pass for uncertain low-risk changes is intended review-policy reduction, not loss of coverage, since merge remains blocked by manual_review_reasons.
